Library force_control_task_lib version 1.0.2.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with eTaSL task specifications for force control tasks for Crospi
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Erwin Aertbeliën (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

is-insertion_action.description:
Task Specification: insertion_action.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description: Insertion action: one step of a force-controlled insertion skill that reduces one degree of freedom (DoF) of the insertion object (held by the robot) w.r.t. the housing object, by a guarded motion until a contact transition is detected (methodology of "Robust Force-Controlled Robotic Insertion Skills for Geometrically Diverse Parts Under Uncertainty", Ulloa Rios et al., CASE 2026). An insertion skill is a sequence of such actions, one per reduced DoF.
The action is specified at the control frame {f_i} (feature_frame, attached to the insertion object at a mating feature, e.g. a corner of a peg). The 6 DoFs are: the translations x, y, z along the axes of the frame {h f_i}, with the origin of {f_i} and the orientation of the housing (housing_orientation), and the rotations rx, ry, rz around the axes of {f_i}. Each DoF is either force controlled (force_controlled = 1) or velocity controlled (0):
- force controlled: admittance towards the target force/torque of target_wrench (Eq. 1 of the paper): velocity = -K_force*(target - measured)/K_t (or /K_r for rotations), limited to maxvel (maxvel_rot). A non-zero target keeps a contact (or, for the reduced DoF, moves towards a new one); a zero target lets the object follow the contact forces (attraction regions);
- velocity controlled: zero velocity (the current offset is kept).
target_wrench is the superposition of the target wrenches of all the mating features, expressed at {f_i}: e.g. a force -F along z at another feature at position r (in {f_i}) adds the force -F along z and the torque r x (0,0,-F). Its sign convention is the wrench exerted by the environment on the insertion object (e.g. pushing with F along the insertion direction z: target -F along z).
The task finishes (monitor action "exit") when, after time_delay, the measured force/torque of the reduced DoF (reduced_dof) reaches monitor_fraction times its target (a contact transition): reduced_dof must be force controlled with a non-zero target.
The measured wrench is read from the input channel named by wrench_input_channel (default "wrench_input") (type wrench, expressed in FT_sensor_frame with its origin as reference point), provided by the robot driver/simulator (e.g. MuJoCo) or by a WrenchInputHandler; it is converted to the wrench exerted on the robot (see wrench_convention), passed through a dead zone, compensated for the tool weight and expressed at {f_i}. Outputs: time, the position of {f_i} (x_f, y_f, z_f), the frames feature_frame ({f_i}) and feature_frame_housing ({h f_i}), and the processed wrench (x_force, y_force, z_force along the axes of {h f_i}; x_torque, y_torque, z_torque around the axes of {f_i}).
Gravity compensation (tool_weight > 0): it assumes that the force/torque sensor was tared with the tool completely vertical, pointing down (the z axis of FT_sensor_frame along gravity, -z of the robot base frame); the tool weight measured in other orientations of the tool is then compensated.

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

FT_sensor_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) of the force/torque sensor. The measured wrench of the input channel (wrench_input_channel) is expressed in this frame, with its origin as reference point

K_r.description: Rotational stiffness [Nm/rad] used as model of the admittance of the force-controlled rotations: the angular velocity is K_force*(measured torque - target)/K_r. Lower values make the rotations faster, higher values slower and stiffer in contact

tool_COG.description: Position [m] of the center of gravity of the tool (everything mounted after the force/torque sensor), as [x,y,z] expressed in FT_sensor_frame. Used for the gravity compensation together with tool_weight

task_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) that is controlled, e.g. the tool center point. The control frame {f_i} is defined w.r.t. this frame by feature_frame

monitor_fraction.description: Fraction delta in (0,1] of the target of the reduced DoF that finishes the task: the task exits when the measured force/torque of reduced_dof divided by its target exceeds it (after time_delay). Lower values detect the contact earlier; 1 may never be reached (the admittance approaches its target asymptotically)

housing_orientation.description: Orientation of the housing feature frame {f_h} (the mating feature of the housing, e.g. the corner of the hole, with z along the insertion direction) w.r.t. the robot base (world) frame, as a unit quaternion [qx,qy,qz,qw] (real part last). The translations and the forces of target_wrench are along the axes of the frame {h f_i}: origin of {f_i}, this orientation

K_force.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the admittance constraints (k_c of Eq. 1 of the paper, related to the bandwidth of the force control). Higher values react faster, but too high values cause oscillations in contact

tool_weight.description: Weight [N] (gravity force, not mass) of the tool mounted after the force/torque sensor, applied at tool_COG, with gravity along -z of the robot base frame. The gravity compensation assumes that the force/torque sensor was tared with the tool completely vertical, pointing down (the z axis of FT_sensor_frame along gravity): it removes the change of the tool weight measured by the sensor when the tool is in another orientation. 0 disables the gravity compensation

maxvel.description: Maximum absolute velocity [m/s] of each force-controlled translation

force_threshold.description: Dead zone [N] applied to each force component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame): components with an absolute value below it are set to zero and larger ones are reduced by it. It suppresses sensor noise and offsets. 0 disables the dead zone

reduced_dof.description: DoF reduced by this action: the force/torque of this DoF is monitored and the task finishes when it reaches monitor_fraction times its target in target_wrench (the contact transition). It must be force controlled, with a non-zero target

wrench_input_channel.description: Name of the input channel (type wrench) from which the measured wrench of the force/torque sensor is read: the varname of the input handler that provides it (e.g. a WrenchInputHandler), or the channel fed directly by the robot driver/simulator (name_expr_cartesian_wrench of the MuJoCo simulator)

feature_frame.description: Pose of the control frame {f_i} (at the mating feature of the insertion object, e.g. a corner of the peg, with z along the insertion direction) w.r.t. task_frame, as [x,y,z,qx,qy,qz,qw] (position in m, unit quaternion with the real part qw last), expressed in task_frame. The torques of target_wrench are w.r.t. its origin and around its axes

force_controlled.description: Control mode of each DoF [x,y,z,rx,ry,rz]: 1 force controlled (admittance towards the element of target_wrench; 0 as target makes the DoF compliant), 0 velocity controlled (zero velocity: the current offset is kept)

wrench_convention.description: Sign convention of the wrench received on the input channel (wrench_input_channel). exerted_on_environment: it is the wrench that the robot exerts on the environment (e.g. the MuJoCo simulator); it is negated. exerted_on_robot: it is the wrench that the environment exerts on the robot and is used as is

torque_threshold.description: Dead zone [Nm] applied to each torque component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame): components with an absolute value below it are set to zero and larger ones are reduced by it. 0 disables the dead zone

K_t.description: Translational stiffness [N/m] used as model of the admittance of the force-controlled translations: the velocity is K_force*(measured force - target)/K_t. Lower values make the guarded motions faster (more velocity for the same force error), higher values slower and stiffer in contact

maxvel_rot.description: Maximum absolute angular velocity [rad/s] of each force-controlled rotation

time_delay.description: Time [s] after the start of the task during which the monitor is disabled, to ignore transients of the forces at the start of the action. 0 activates it immediately

target_wrench.description: Target wrench [Fx,Fy,Fz,Tx,Ty,Tz] ([N] along the axes of {h f_i}, [Nm] around the axes of {f_i}, w.r.t. the origin of {f_i}) of the force-controlled DoFs: the superposition of the target wrenches of all the mating features, in the sign convention of the wrench exerted by the environment on the insertion object (e.g. -F along z pushes with F along the insertion direction). The elements of velocity-controlled DoFs are ignored
